title: Tunes made up on the club stand, and publishers copying them onto their cuffs
summary: After hours at the club the band built tunes from Fats's chords while publishers like Archie Bleyer wrote them down and sold them back as stock arrangements.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Herman, when Fats was playing these games with the publishers, with the checkbook, and everything, did -- was -- were you making up a lot of tunes right on the stand there? Did he just sort of start playing something, and people -- the rest of you'd get in on it?

No, not to -- no. No, not then. Not then. But I mean that did happen throughout the night. I mean after. Because when you're recording, or broadcasting, you want to be -- sound together. Want to be together, thinkingwise, playing. You know. Because you can't take too many shots in -- you don't know when you might miss, and that's bad. Yeah, you know.
Right, but in other words, you didn't do it for recording or on the air, but in the club you --

In the club you sit there, and you start -- guys who -- what's this? And Fats say well B flat, or C sharp, or -- he'd hit the chords, and so and so and so and so. And he would take one. He would say I've got it! I've got the first one by myself, and he would play, and you would listen, see the progressions, how the progressions go, chords and whatnot. And when you got ready you'd fall in. If not you, me, another guy. And you still listened. And you'd say gee, I'd like to have some of that. I had some ideas. I'd like to try.
So you come in with your ideas, and they might be

terrific. And it move from you, to the other guy, one guy will do something, will make that wow! You say man, listen to that! And it might be some other musicians in there, or publishers, something like -- what the hell is that? What was that? Do it again. Oh man, and then you'd get -- I'd put it on paper, and getting ready to sell it to him, because he's going to sell it right back to you at the end of the week, because he -- (laughs). They'll raise it, and it'll come out in the stock form. See?

He worked with Arthur Godfrey for a while. You know who I'm talking about? (Snaps fingers.) The publisher? Wrote more tunes, what was that? Hmmm, hmmm, hmmmmm, made millions, guy with tunes, and he's arranger here. He -- Martin Block. Not Martin Block.
I remember Archie Bleyer, if that's the guy you're talking -- Archie Bleyer?

Archie used to come in the club. He -- I can name you so many sitting there writing on the cuffs of their shirt. Him, me, and some other guy makes something, and you see them sitting there with pen and pencil doing this, and --
Sure. And they'd go back, back to his
office, and when you go down there to buy a tune, you buy -- you say man! That looks familiar. Isn't it nice? And that stuff's some of the same stuff they're selling back to us.
That you played last week, and it's your own thing.

And I would -- if you don't see that stuff in print, uh, you don't recognize it. You don't -- you've got to be mighty smart a man to recognize just what's happening, you know, and that's what they did.
